title: Over Tiquiná Creek
story:
The narrow dirt path led James away from the stone aqueduct and into a rich mosaic of quiet, terraced farmland. He walked past high stalks of green maize whispering in the morning breeze. He walked past damp rows of leafy squash blossom vines clinging to the fertile dark earth. He walked past ancient stone low walls where small blue wildflowers peered out from mortar cracks. The air here was soft and rich with the damp, earthy scent of turned soil and wild marigolds, so different from the polished cedar and old ink of the Grand Library, yet comforting in its own grounded way.

As the dirt trail dipped down toward a rushing mountain stream known as Tiquiná Creek, James paused atop a small arched stone footbridge. The icy water below tumbled rapidly over smooth river stones, clear as mountain air. Resting his paws on the mossy stone balustrade, James unclipped his small brass compass from his chest strap. He watched the slender needle wobble, spin, and settle once more toward the south. Fifty-three days ago, he had known only the tangled shadows of the Great Canopy; now, every step carried him further into a world far larger than any single map could hold.

Taking out his piece of green sea-glass, James held it up to his right eye, gazing through its smooth tint at the sunlit creek and the soft blue contours of the distant southern hills. The rushing water turned a brilliant shade of deep jade, shimmering like the canal waters beneath Weaver's Wharf. He tucked the glass safely back beside his brass map canister, feeling the comforting weight of his collected treasures rest against his side. Every small object was a thread tethering him to the places he had walked and the friends who had welcomed him along the way.

Crossing to the far side of the footbridge, James sat down for a moment on a smooth, sun-warmed boulder beside a weathered wooden waystation marker. He adjusted the leather strap across his chest, feeling the steady warmth of the morning sun on his fur. Ahead, the dirt trail curved gently around a pine-crowned hill, leading deeper into the valley. "Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next," James whispered softly to the open road ahead, watching a single floating leaf drift down the current and out of sight.
location: An arched stone footbridge over Tiquiná Creek
